name: xPin Plugin Directory
installNote: Packages install through xPin's review queue: Plugins → Marketplace → Install → Review → Approve. Nothing runs before you approve it.

plugins.name: Backlinks Quick
plugins.description: Work with backlinks to the current note: count them, or cycle through them one at a time.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Backlinks Quick

Backlink helpers for the note you have open. A "backlink" is any note whose
body contains `[[<your note's title>]]`.

## Commands

- **Count backlinks** — toasts how many notes link to the current note.
- **Jump to next backlink** — opens the next note that links here, cycling
  through all of them and wrapping around. The position in the cycle is kept
  in the plugin's settings, so it survives restarts and switching notes
  (each note gets its own cycle position).

## Permissions used

`commands:register`, `notes:read`, `notes:select`, `ui:notify`,
`settings:read`, `settings:write`

## Notes for builders

- `[[Title]]` matching is an exact, case-sensitive substring match on the
  note body, using a literal (non-regex) search.
- The cycle key is `backlinkIndex:<noteId>` so positions don't collide.

plugins.name: Case Converter
plugins.description: Convert the current note's title and body to UPPERCASE, lowercase, or Title Case via three commands.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Case Converter

Three command-palette commands that transform the **title and body** of the
note currently open in the editor, in place:

- **UPPERCASE note** — everything to upper case
- **lowercase note** — everything to lower case
- **Title Case note** — first letter of each word capitalized

Each command confirms with a short toast (or reports the error). The
transformation is applied via `notes:update`, so it respects the app's
normal note-update path (history, sync, re-render).

Permissions: `notes:read`, `notes:update`, `commands:register`, `ui:notify`.

plugins.name: Daily Word Goal
plugins.description: Tracks words written today across all notes and cheers when you hit your daily goal.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Daily Word Goal

A daily writing target across all your notes.

**Commands:** `Set daily word goal` (cycles 100/250/500/1000/2000), `Refresh goal progress`.

**How it works:** every 30s it sums the words in notes created or updated today and shows `312/500 words today` in the status bar. The first time the total reaches the goal each day, you get a celebration toast (tracked with a per-day flag, local time). Goal persists in plugin settings.

Pack: `node plugins/pack.mjs plugins/oem/daily-goal`

plugins.name: Duplicate Titles
plugins.description: Scan all notes for duplicate titles and report the count and duplicated titles in a toast.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Duplicate Titles

One command-palette command: **Find duplicate titles**.

Scans every note (up to 500 via `notes:list()`), groups by normalized
title (trimmed, case-insensitive — "Ideas" and "ideas" are duplicates),
and reports via toast, e.g.:

`3 duplicate titles: Ideas, Meeting notes, +1 more`

The title list is truncated so the whole message always fits the
200-character toast limit. Untitled notes are skipped.

Permissions: `notes:read`, `commands:register`, `ui:notify`.

plugins.name: Link Checker
plugins.description: Scan every note for [[wiki-links]] whose target title doesn't exist, and report the broken ones.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Link Checker

Find dead `[[wiki-links]]` in your notes.

## Commands

- **Find broken links** — scans every note body for `[[Some Title]]`
  references whose target doesn't match any existing note's exact title,
  then toasts the count plus the first 2–3 broken targets so you can fix them.

## Permissions used

`commands:register`, `notes:read`, `ui:notify`

## Notes for builders

- Wikilinks are extracted with a simple regex (`/\[\[([^\][]+)\]\]/g`);
  targets are trimmed and matched exactly (case-sensitive) against titles.
- Dedupe targets so each broken link is counted once, and sort them for a
  stable, readable report.

plugins.name: Meeting Notes
plugins.description: Creates a dated meeting note with attendees, agenda, notes and action items sections, then opens it.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Meeting Notes

One command to be meeting-ready.

**Commands:** `New meeting note`.

**How it works:** creates a note titled `Meeting — <today's date>` with Attendees / Agenda / Notes / Action items sections, opens it in the editor, and confirms with a toast. Minimal permissions by design.

Pack: `node plugins/pack.mjs plugins/oem/meeting-notes`

plugins.name: Note Streak
plugins.description: Shows your consecutive-days note-writing streak in the status bar.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Note Streak

Your consecutive-days writing streak in the status bar.

**Commands:** `Show streak details` (current streak, longest streak, total notes).

**How it works:** refreshes every 60s — a day counts when at least one note was created on it (local time). If today has no notes yet, the streak counts back from yesterday so you aren't reset mid-morning. All date math is DST-safe.

Pack: `node plugins/pack.mjs plugins/oem/note-streak`

plugins.name: Pomodoro Focus Timer
plugins.description: Pomodoro focus and break timers with status-bar countdown and adjustable durations.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Pomodoro Focus Timer

A Pomodoro timer in the xPin status bar.

**Commands:** `Start focus (25m)`, `Start break (5m)`, `Stop timer`, `Set focus length` (cycles 15/25/45/60 min), `Set break length` (cycles 5/10/15 min).

**How it works:** a 1-second worker-side interval updates the status bar (`Focus 24:59`); when the session ends you get a toast and the timer clears itself. Durations persist in plugin settings. Starting a new timer always replaces the running one. Disabling the plugin stops the interval.

Pack: `node plugins/pack.mjs plugins/oem/pomodoro-focus`

plugins.name: Random Note
plugins.description: Jump to a uniformly random note with a single command — serendipitous rediscovery for your note collection.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Random Note

Jump to a **uniformly random note** from your whole collection with a single
command-palette action. A nice way to rediscover old ideas.

## Commands

- **Open random note** — picks one note at random and opens it in the editor,
  notifying you of its title. If you have no notes yet, you get a toast saying
  so instead.

## Permissions used

`commands:register`, `notes:read`, `notes:select`, `ui:notify`

## Notes for builders

- The draw uses `Math.random()` against the full list returned by
  `api.notes.list()` (up to 500 notes), so every note is equally likely.
- Every `run()` is wrapped in `try/catch` so failures surface as toasts.

plugins.name: Reading List
plugins.description: A simple read-later queue: add the current note, cycle through it round-robin, and check its size.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Reading List

A simple **read-later queue** stored in the plugin's settings.

## Commands

- **Add current note to reading list** — queues the open note. Duplicates
  are skipped, so adding the same note twice won't pile up.
- **Open next in reading list** — opens the head of the queue, then rotates
  it to the back (round-robin). Notes that were deleted in the meantime are
  dropped automatically.
- **Reading list size** — toasts how many notes are queued (after cleaning
  out any that no longer exist).

## Permissions used

`commands:register`, `notes:read`, `notes:select`, `ui:notify`,
`settings:read`, `settings:write`

## Notes for builders

- The queue is an array of note ids under the `queue` settings key.
- `notes:select` on the head of the queue is only ever done after verifying
  the id still exists in `notes:list()`.

plugins.name: Reading Time
plugins.description: Shows a live reading-time estimate (200 words per minute) for the current note in the status bar.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Reading Time

Live reading-time estimate for the note currently open in the editor,
shown in the status bar and refreshed every 2 seconds.

- **Status item id:** `reading-time`
- **Rate:** 200 words per minute; rounds up, minimum "1 min read"
  for any non-empty note.
- Cleared automatically when no note is open.

Permissions: `notes:read`, `ui:status`.

plugins.name: Table Formatter
plugins.description: Align markdown pipe tables in the current note by padding cells to equal column widths.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Table Formatter

One command-palette command: **Format markdown tables**.

Scans the body of the note currently open in the editor for GitHub-flavored
pipe tables (consecutive `|…|` lines with a `---` separator row) and
rewrites each with columns padded to equal widths so the raw markdown
lines up, e.g.:

```
| Name  | Age |
| ----- | --- |
| Ada   | 36  |
| Grace | 85  |
```

Alignment markers (`:---`, `---:`, `:---:`) are preserved. Blocks that
aren't valid tables (ragged columns, no separator row) are left untouched.
The toast reports how many tables were formatted, or "No tables found."

Permissions: `notes:read`, `notes:update`, `commands:register`, `ui:notify`.

plugins.name: Tag Manager
plugins.description: Tag census report plus a generated tag index note, from your #hashtags.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Tag Manager

Audit your `#hashtag` usage across all notes.

## Commands

- **Tag census** — counts distinct `#tags` across all notes and toasts the
  total plus the top 5 by usage, e.g. `12 tags · top: #work(8), #ideas(5), …`.
- **Create tag index note** — writes a "Tag index" note listing every tag
  with its note count, most-used first, and opens it.

## Permissions used

`commands:register`, `notes:create`, `notes:read`, `ui:notify`

## Notes for builders

- xPin has no `note.tags` field: tags are `#hashtags` in the title/body text,
  extracted with the host's own pattern `/(?:^|\s)#([a-z0-9][a-z0-9/_-]*)/gi`
  and lowercased, so the census agrees with xPin's tag filter.
- Renaming a tag would need a prompt API (which doesn't exist), so this
  plugin reports and indexes instead of renaming.
- Toast text is kept under the 200-char limit by truncating the top-5 list.

plugins.name: Template Inserter
plugins.description: Insert ready-made markdown skeletons — meeting, daily log, decision record, book notes — at the cursor.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Template Inserter

Four markdown skeletons at the cursor.

**Commands:** `Insert meeting template`, `Insert daily log template`, `Insert decision record`, `Insert book notes template`.

**How it works:** each inserts a compact, dated skeleton via `editor:write`. If no note is open, the insert creates one. No notes are read and no settings are stored.

Pack: `node plugins/pack.mjs plugins/oem/template-inserter`

plugins.name: Text Statistics
plugins.description: Two commands: a one-line text statistics summary as a toast, and a full markdown statistics report inserted at the cursor.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Text Statistics

Two command-palette commands for the note currently open in the editor:

1. **Show text statistics** — a compact one-line toast:
   `123 words · 456 chars · 7 sentences · 3 paragraphs`
2. **Insert statistics report** — writes a fuller markdown table report
   (words, characters with/without spaces, sentences, paragraphs, lines)
   at the cursor position.

Both commands are fully automatic (no dialogs exist in the sandbox) and
report failures as toasts instead of failing silently.

Permissions: `notes:read`, `commands:register`, `ui:notify`, `editor:write`.

plugins.name: Untagged Finder
plugins.description: Find notes with no tags: count them, or cycle through them one at a time for tagging.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Untagged Finder

Hunt down notes that have no `#hashtags`.

## Commands

- **Count untagged notes** — toasts how many notes contain no `#tag`.
- **Open next untagged note** — opens the next untagged note, cycling through
  all of them and wrapping around, so you can tag them one by one. The cycle
  position is stored in settings and survives restarts.

## Permissions used

`commands:register`, `notes:read`, `notes:select`, `ui:notify`,
`settings:read`, `settings:write`

## Notes for builders

- A note is "untagged" when its title+body contain no `#hashtag` matching the
  host's tag pattern `/(?:^|\s)#([a-z0-9][a-z0-9/_-]*)/gi` (xPin has no
  `note.tags` field — tags are inline in the text).
- The cycle order is by `updatedAt` (newest first) and the stored index is
  normalized with modulo, so deleted/retagged notes can't break it.

plugins.name: Word Sprint
plugins.description: Timed writing sprints: hit a word-count target in the open note before the clock runs out.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Word Sprint

Timed writing sprints on the open note.

**Commands:** `Start word sprint`, `Stop word sprint`, `Set sprint word target` (100/300/500/750/1000), `Set sprint length` (5/10/15/25/30 min).

**How it works:** starting a sprint snapshots the open note's word count; the status bar shows `123/300 · 12:34 left` as you write. Hit the target and you're congratulated; run out of time and you get your final tally. Switching to a different note mid-sprint shows "paused" instead of counting the wrong note.

Pack: `node plugins/pack.mjs plugins/oem/word-sprint`

plugins.name: Word Tally
plugins.description: Shows live word and character counts of the current note in the status bar, updating every 2 seconds.
plugins.author: xPin OEM
plugins.readme:
# Word Tally

Live word + character count of the note currently open in the editor,
shown in the status bar and refreshed every 2 seconds.

- **Status item id:** `word-tally`
- **Format:** `12 words · 345 chars`
- The item is cleared automatically when no note is open.
- Poll failures are swallowed silently; the next tick retries.

Permissions: `notes:read`, `ui:status`.
